subject: Proposed week-of cadence for hands-on prompt lab + load test backstop
thread_content:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@blueleaf.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara@netzo.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed week-of cadence for hands-on prompt lab + load test backstop

Hi Dylan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Blueleaf is excited to move to a hands-on session where we can walk our engineers through a set of live prompts and run a short load window to validate request patterns.

High level ask: can Redwood run a 2-day workshop the week of July 6 where Day 1 is a focused prompt inventory + guardrail alignment (2–3 hours), and Day 2 is a hands-on routing/load window (3 hours) with the option for a short follow-up the following week? We also need a backstop for the load test in case we see regressions — ideally a rollback path or temporary throttling policy.

Attached is our initial prompt inventory (CSV) and a simple traffic sketch. Can you share availability and the earliest safe load window? Also confirm any credentials/IP allowlisting you need.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Hayes
Head of Platform, Blueleaf AI

--
Attachments: prompt_inventory_v1.csv (CSV, 42KB), traffic_sketch.png (PNG, 180KB)

---
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@blueleaf.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed week-of cadence for hands-on prompt lab + load test backstop

Tom —

Really glad the demo landed. We can absolutely run the two-part workshop and the load window. A few quick things up front so we can commit calendar slots:

- Day 1 (Prompt inventory + guardrails): recommend a 2.5 hr slot. Goal: agree canonical prompt set, structured-output schemas, and what rolling validations look like.
- Day 2 (Hands-on routing + load window): 3 hr with an agreed 60-min load window in the middle. We’ll run a gradual ramp (25% -> 100%) and have an on-call fallback plan (throttle to 30 RPS or failover to a smaller model) if we detect latency or quality regressions.
- Pre-reqs: allowlist IPs for our test agents, a service account key (we’ll provide a token exchange flow if you prefer not to hand over keys), and a short list of top-50 prompts from your CSV.

Availability at our end: Tue Jul 6 AM PT (9–12) or Thu Jul 8 PM PT (13–16) for Day 1; Wed Jul 7 10–14 PT or Fri Jul 9 09–12 PT for Day 2. If you prefer a contiguous two-day block we can do Jul 6–7 in the AM.

I’m looping Ben and Karthik — Ben will lead ops for the load window and Karthik will run the prompt/structuring session.

Cheers,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@blueleaf.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed week-of cadence for hands-on prompt lab + load test backstop

Quick ops note from my side:

- For the load window, we need a calendar slot that includes 30 minutes before the ramp to validate warm caches, followed by the 60-min ramped load, then 30–45 minutes of soak/verification. So please plan for ~2.25–2.5 hrs for Day 2.
- We’ll bring a fallback policy: immediate throttle (per-customer token cap) + instant model downgrade to a quantized variant if latency > 450ms p50 for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Please attach the list of 50 test prompts as a plain text file (not CSV) — we parse less predictably from some spreadsheets.

I’ll also need the IP allowlist at least 48 hours before the run and an emergency Slack channel for the blueleaf engineering contacts.

-Ben

From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@blueleaf.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed week-of cadence for hands-on prompt lab + load test backstop

Thanks team — 2 quick clarifications:

1) We can do Jul 6–7 contiguous AM block. That fits our calendar.
2) We’ll provide the top-50 prompts as plain text and add an architecture diagram to the Drive folder.

Also — on the rollback/backstop: are there any compliance steps we need to pre-approve to allow temporary throttling (this would impact some downstream metrics)? If so share the form and we’ll escalate.

Tom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@blueleaf.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed week-of cadence for hands-on prompt lab + load test backstop

Tom —

We don’t require any formal compliance sign-off just to run the throttling policy during the window; it’s an operational control we’ll enact unilaterally for the load test. That said, if you want a written note for your ops team we can provide a short override authorization template. I’ve attached a draft in this thread.

I’ll also prepare a short guardrails checklist for Day 1: allowed tokens, structured output examples (JSON schemas), redaction guidance, and a list of success/failure signals to watch.

-Karthik

Attachments: throttle-authorization-template.pdf, guardrails-checklist.md
